Social Media Remodel · Prepared by Jake for Shavit Rootman

What your socials
become.

You’re already on Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn and Substack, and every one still reads as the personal Shavit that went quiet in February. This rebuilds all of them, plus a Meta Business Suite cockpit and a YouTube channel to establish, into one real-estate operator brand, using footage and photos we already made, on a calm 2 to 3-post-a-week rhythm. Instagram is the deep-dive (it’s the flagship); Section 02 covers the full footprint. Reputation, not noise.

Now YouTube, not established yet

There’s no channel today. The value prop already names YouTube as a home for the signature film alongside IG and TikTok, right now that home doesn’t exist.

Revised What changes

Establish the channel as the long-form house: the brand film pinned, plus full before/after project tours that don’t fit in a 60-second reel. The one place the whole story runs start to finish.

Lowest urgency of the six, stand it up when the first long cut is ready. Until then it holds the brand film and the handle, so the name is claimed.
One link, one order. Every bio points to shavitrootman.com/links, a single branded link page (no third-party logo) listing, in this order: Website → Facebook → LinkedIn → Substack. Change a destination once, it updates everywhere.
03 · THE TRANSITION

How we revamp without going blank

The #1 worry with a rebrand: “do we wipe 57 posts and start from an empty grid?” No. We never delete in bulk, and the account is never blank for a single day. The trick is to layer new on top first, then quietly retire the old, and on Instagram you Archive (hide, fully reversible) rather than delete, so nothing is ever lost.

DAY 1

Reframe, remove nothing

Switch to Business, swap the bio, add the 5 highlights, and re-pin the top 3. Every old post still sits there, but the first impression is already the new brand. A 20-minute change that makes the account feel reborn without touching the grid.

WEEKS 1-4

Layer new on top

Start posting the branded content, 2-3×/week. New posts land at the top, so the grid fills up and drifts the old stuff down naturally. Post count goes up, never down.

WEEKS 3-8

Quietly retire, matched 1:1

As branded rows build, Archive 2-3 weak old posts a week, only as fast as new ones go up. The total count stays flat-to-climbing, the grid is never patchy, and archived posts are recoverable (and re-usable).

BY WEEK 12

One operation, top to bottom

The top 3-4 rows are fully branded. Anything below is either archived or intentionally kept. The account reads as one operation, and it was never once blank along the way.

Watch the grid, week by week

Left to right: the same account, transforming. New branded posts (gold/brass tiles) fill from the top; the striped tiles are your existing posts, retiring a few at a time. Notice the post count only ever climbs.

The keep / reformat / archive rule

✓ Keep

Genuine property before/afters & finished-home carousels. On-brand already, we just reformat them into the template over time.

♻ Reformat

Strong stories shot in low quality. Re-edit the good ones into the new template and re-post as fresh content.

⤓ Archive

Random, off-brand, or low-quality one-offs. Hidden (not deleted), a few a week, only as new posts replace them.

🇮🇱 Re-home

The Israel & family posts move into the “Roots” highlight, the human story stays visible without leading the grid.

Net effect: on any given day a visitor sees a full, on-brand grid. There is no “under construction” phase, the revamp happens live and invisibly, one post at a time.

05 · HIGHLIGHTS

Five highlights that do the selling

Highlights are the permanent menu under your bio. Five, each with a brass-ringed cover, so a first-time visitor can navigate your whole story in five taps.

ON FILM

The reels. Brand film first, then every cinematic cut. A stranger taps here to see the operation move.

HOUSES

The photos. Finished rooms and finished homes, the way they look the day someone moves in.

THE WORK

The renovations. Studs, dust, and the reveal. Shot on a phone, straight from the job site.

ROOTS

The human thread, Shavit, the Rootman clan, Israel. Kept and re-homed here (not scrubbed): authenticity the 5k base already follows him for.

AVAILABLE

What’s available, and how to reach him. The only highlight that asks for anything.

06 · CONTENT PILLARS

What we post, and how often

Five pillars keep the grid varied without ever guessing what to post. The mix leans on transformations (they get saved and shared the most) while keeping the mission and the human side in frame.

40%

Transformations

Before → after reveals. The signature format and the highest-save content. Two matched photos = one post.

25%

Portfolio & operator POV

Reels, walkthroughs, “inside the operation.” Proof of scale: three states, one crew.

15%

The mission

Second-chance housing, community, dignity. The reputation layer, why this operation is different.

10%

The human / roots

Shavit, the team, Israel, behind-the-scenes. The authenticity your 5k base already follows you for.

10%

Education / market

“BRRRR, explained.” “What it cost / what it became.” Quiet authority that ages well.

07 · THE 90-DAY REACTIVATION

A calm relaunch, 2-3 posts a week

No explosion. A steady reactivation of the base you already have. Weekly template: a transformation early week, a portfolio/education mid-week, and an optional mission/human post to close it out. Light Stories 2-3× a week.

08 · HOW WE'LL MEASURE IT

The numbers this feeds

Reputation is the goal, so these are the signals we track, measured over a 6-month window, reported to you monthly. These are targets and method, not promises, real figures start the day the account switches to Business and Insights turn on.

Cadence adherence
100% of planned posts ship

The controllable win. A 2-week buffer means the brand never goes quiet again.

Engagement rate
Hold & lift vs today

Current likes run ~1.6-2.3% of followers. Before/afters carry the highest save rate, lead with them.

Saves + shares
The reputation signal

Saves & shares matter more than likes for a brand play. Tracked monthly.

Reach reactivation
Lift vs dormant baseline

Waking the 5,054 base and measuring the climb over 90 days.

Inbound logged
DMs · mentions · “saw your stuff”

Every inbound screenshotted, the evidence that reputation is actually moving.

Followers (net new)
Secondary

Nice, not the point. Reputation over raw growth, exactly as we agreed.

Everything here honors the plan we set: maintenance and reputation, not virality. The goal is an account that looks alive, on-brand, and never goes quiet, the two things that actually can’t be faked: taste and reliability.
